organization.discoveryNotes: Retail operating model pack (F32): multi-store ops, catalog/inventory readiness, POS boundary awareness (no live payments), returns/promotions, and reconciliation workflows. Confirm store count, online vs physical mix, and reporting needs.

workflows.name: Stock receiving
workflows.description: DC or store receiving with inventory controller sign-off.

workflows.name: Inventory count / stock adjustment
workflows.description: Cycle count with manager approval on variances.

workflows.name: Return / exchange review
workflows.description: Customer service intake; store manager and finance review for exceptions.

workflows.name: Discount / promotion approval
workflows.description: Marketing proposes; operations and finance approve before store rollout.

workflows.name: Cash reconciliation
workflows.description: Daily till reconciliation with finance review trail.

workflows.name: Supplier purchase request
workflows.description: Buyer submits replenishment PO; finance approves above threshold.

securityRequirements.requirement: POS and back-office role separation (operator policy)
Payment data boundary — no card data in Crow (advisory)
Audit trail on price, discount, and stock adjustments
Refund and return approval evidence readiness

integrations.notes: Staff SSO for HQ and store back-office (future operator setup)

experienceRequirements.requirement: Revenue, margin, stock-outs, store health, risk posture
Store and operations dashboards with approvals and exceptions
Task list, escalations, POS guidance — minimal navigation
Reports, trends, evidence gaps — no payment processing UI

identity.ssoNotes: Retail template: MFA for managers recommended; store associates via managed accounts. E-commerce MFA risk is future security reference only.

security.complianceNotes: Customer PII in CRM; segment store staff from finance roles. PCI DSS is advisory reference only if payment data is ever handled outside Crow.
